title: New 'Blue Zone' of Long-Lived People Found in Sardinia
paragraphs: If you want to know where people live the longest, look no farther than our planet's "blue zones."

"Blue zones" are areas where people live unusually long, healthy lives. There are only six of them around the world, including Okinawa in Japan and the Greek island of Ikaria — while Singapore was just added to the list in 2023.
The first blue zone was identified on the Italian island of Sardinia in 2004 — a cluster of mountain villages in the eastern part of the island.
Now, 22 years later, researchers believe they may have found a second blue zone on Sardinia — a village called Bolotana in the center of the island, about 110 kilometers from that first blue zone.

Researchers studied the village between 2021 and 2025. During this time, the village had a population of about 2,300 people, among whom 10 were aged 100 or older — putting the proportion of centenarians at 442 out of 100,000.
Okinawa, meanwhile, now has 1,192 centenarians — giving it a proportion of 81 out of 100,000.

The researchers found that men who reached the age of 70 in Bolotana had an average life expectancy of 16 more years, while for women it was almost 21 more years. And 5% of 70-year-old men even survived until they were 100 — while 14% of women did the same.

Looking to explain why people in Bolotana might enjoy such longevity, the researchers found that the local diet is about 90% plant-based, with people mostly producing their own food, and meat eaten only about five times a month.
The village is also very hilly, and few people have cars, so everyone gets lots of exercise just walking around every day.
But while women globally generally live three to five years longer than men, the researchers aren't sure why women in Bolotana are so much more likely than men to reach 100!
